speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are presenting with postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass; to determine the underlying cause, I need to ask you a few specific questions. First, how old are you, and when was your last menstrual period?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Regarding the adnexal mass, could you describe its specific characteristics, such as whether it appears complex or solid on imaging, and have you had any prior gynecological surgeries? Also, have you experienced any pelvic pain or pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic Ultrasound (transvaginal).
DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Hyperplasia secondary to Unopposed Estrogen from an Ovarian Sex Cord-Stromal Tumor (e.g., Granulosa Cell Tumor).
